title: 7 signs of an unsafe adventure operator
hook: Check this before you pay for any adventure.
caption: Great adventures start with a safe operator. Save this checklist, screenshot it, and send it to whoever is booking your next trip.
altText: A nine-slide checklist of seven warning signs that an adventure operator is not safe — no briefing, worn gear, untrained guides, no weather check, too many people per guide, nothing in writing, and no first-aid plan — each with the question to ask before you pay.

slides.title: Check this before you pay for any adventure.
slides.body: Seven signs an operator is cutting corners, and the question to ask about each one.

slides.title: No safety briefing before you start
slides.body: A good operator tells you what happens before you get in the water or on the rope, not after.

callout.label: Ask
callout.text: What will you cover with us before we go in?

slides.title: Gear that is worn, missing or does not fit
slides.body: Life jackets and helmets only work in the right size, and frayed straps are a decision someone already made.

callout.label: Ask
callout.text: Can I see and try the gear before we start?

slides.title: Guides with no stated training
slides.body: Certifications are not a formality here. An operator who has them will say so without being pushed.

callout.label: Ask
callout.text: Who is leading, and what are their certifications?

slides.title: No weather or water check on the day
slides.body: Conditions decide whether a session happens. An operator who never cancels is telling you something.

slides.title: Too many people per guide
slides.body: One guide watching fifteen beginners cannot reach you quickly. Smaller groups cost more for a reason.

slides.title: Nothing in writing before you pay
slides.body: Inclusions, timings and the cancellation terms should exist somewhere other than a conversation.

callout.label: Ask
callout.text: Can you send this in writing?

slides.title: No first-aid kit or emergency plan
slides.body: Ask where the nearest hospital is. If nobody knows, that is the answer.

callout.label: Ask
callout.text: What is the plan if someone is hurt?

slides.title: Save this before your next booking.
slides.body: Send it to whoever is planning your next trip.

actions.label: Send it to your trip group

notes: Nothing here is a factual claim about a named operator, which is deliberate: it is general guidance any instructor would agree with, so it carries no verification risk. Keep it that way — naming operators turns this into a recommendation.
